name: Haichang Ocean Park Holdings
desc: Operates marine-themed amusement and aquarium parks in China, selling tickets, food, merchandise and hotel stays to families and tourists.
markets: Parks in several Chinese cities; customers are Chinese families and tourists. No verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Mass-market Chinese leisure brand with little overseas presence; any F1 tie would mainly be a domestic consumer-awareness play.

name: Vestaron
desc: Develops peptide-based biological insecticides for vegetables, fruit and row crops, sold to growers through distributors and crop protection firms.
markets: Sells crop protection products to growers, mainly in the United States; no confirmed operations elsewhere or expansion plans.
rationale: B2B farm input brand known only to growers and agronomists; little consumer marketing culture, so F1 fit is weak.

name: AVAX One Technology
desc: Formerly AgriFORCE Growing Systems, now a Nasdaq-listed company holding a treasury of Avalanche (AVAX) cryptocurrency tokens.
markets: Small listed company with a crypto-token treasury; no verified customers or operations abroad and no known expansion plans.
rationale: Crypto firms do sponsor F1, but this is a small treasury vehicle with no consumer brand, so fit is weak.
changed: Renamed from AgriFORCE Growing Systems to AVAX One in 2025

name: Salmon Evolution
desc: Builds and runs land-based recirculating aquaculture farms in Norway, farming Atlantic salmon for sale to seafood buyers.
markets: Farm at Indre Haroy, Norway; salmon sold to export markets, mainly Europe and Asia. Expansion within Norway planned.
rationale: Seafood producer with premium-protein positioning, but commodity salmon sold B2B; limited brand-marketing need and modest F1 fit.

name: Muyuan Foods
desc: China's largest hog producer, raising pigs across Chinese provinces and selling live hogs, piglets and feed to slaughterhouses and farms.
markets: Operations and customers in China only; no verified overseas operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Commodity pork producer selling to processors with minimal consumer branding; F1 partnership offers little commercial logic.

name: Afresh
desc: Provides AI software that helps supermarket chains forecast demand and order fresh produce, meat and bakery items to cut waste.
markets: Customers are US supermarket chains; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: AI-for-retail technology with enterprise grocery buyers; F1 could showcase AI credentials, but customers are US grocers, so fit is modest.

name: American AgCredit
desc: Borrower-owned Farm Credit System lender financing farms, ranches and agribusinesses with loans and leases in northern California and neighbouring states.
markets: Lends to farmers and ranchers in a handful of western US states; no international activity.
rationale: Regional member-owned farm lender with no mass-market brand; F1 spend would be hard to justify to members.

name: Hoa Phat Group
desc: Vietnam's largest private steelmaker, producing construction steel, hot-rolled coil and pipes, with additional agriculture and real estate businesses.
markets: Sells mainly in Vietnam, with exports to other Asian markets and Europe; Dung Quat steel complex supports growth.
rationale: Large Vietnamese industrial brand seeking regional profile; steel is mostly B2B, so F1 fit is plausible but not obvious.

name: Keurig Green Mountain
desc: Makes single-serve Keurig brewers and K-Cup pods and sells coffee under brands including Green Mountain Coffee Roasters.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States and Canada; part of Keurig Dr Pepper since the 2018 merger.
rationale: Mass-market coffee brand with big consumer reach, but US and Canada focus and a parent group handling sponsorship.
changed: Acquired by JAB in 2016; merged with Dr Pepper Snapple to form Keurig Dr Pepper in 2018

name: Camposol
desc: Peruvian agribusiness that grows, packs and exports fresh avocados, blueberries, mandarins, grapes and asparagus to supermarkets in several world regions.
markets: Exports to North America, Europe and Asia from Peruvian farms; customers are supermarkets and importers.
rationale: Export-led fresh produce brand selling B2B to retailers; F1 hospitality could help retail relationships, but the fit is weak.

name: Vivescia
desc: French farmer-owned cooperative group collecting cereals and processing them into malt, flour, starch and ingredients for food and brewing customers.
markets: Farmer-members in Champagne; malt and flour exports to brewers and food makers in Europe and other regions.
rationale: Farmer cooperative with a largely B2B ingredients business; brewing-customer hospitality has some appeal, but overall F1 fit is weak.

name: Cristal Union
desc: French sugar-beet cooperative owned by growers, operating sugar factories and producing white sugar, alcohol and bioethanol.
markets: Sugar factories in France; sells sugar and alcohol to food and industrial customers, mainly in Europe.
rationale: Cooperative with consumer sugar brands in France but a commodity focus; limited marketing case for F1.

name: Hello Group (Momo)
desc: Operates the Momo location-based social and live-video app and the Tantan dating app, earning revenue from virtual gifts and subscriptions.
markets: Apps used mainly in China, with Tantan and other apps also reaching overseas users; Nasdaq-listed.
rationale: Large consumer app brand with some overseas expansion; F1 could reach a young audience, though marketing focus is mainly China.
changed: Renamed Hello Group in 2021

name: Benson Hill
desc: Food-technology company that used a crop-design platform to produce high-protein soybeans and ingredients such as pea and soy proteins.
markets: Customers were US food and feed manufacturers; the business was wound down after bankruptcy.
rationale: Business ceased after bankruptcy, leaving no active brand to market; no F1 case.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2025 and sold its assets

name: Bowery Farming
desc: Operated indoor vertical farms growing leafy greens and herbs with robotics and software, sold under the Bowery brand.
markets: Sold produce through US grocers and retailers; the company shut down in 2024.
rationale: Company has closed down, so there is no active brand to partner with and no F1 case.
changed: Ceased operations in 2024

name: LAXEY
desc: Plans large land-based recirculating aquaculture capacity for Atlantic salmon on Iceland's Westman Islands.
markets: Pre-revenue project in Iceland; intended to supply European and US markets once harvests begin.
rationale: Pre-revenue fish farm project with no consumer brand and an Icelandic base; weak F1 fit.

name: Ghana Cocoa Board
desc: State regulator and trader of Ghana's cocoa, buying beans from farmers, setting farm-gate prices and selling to chocolate makers.
markets: Sells Ghanaian cocoa beans to chocolate makers and traders in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Government body managing a commodity export crop; F1 sponsorship is unlikely given its public-sector mandate.

name: Nocera
desc: Designs recirculating aquaculture systems and offers fish-farming consulting, serving fish farmers in Asia and Africa.
markets: Projects in Taiwan and elsewhere in Asia and Africa; Nasdaq-listed small-cap.
rationale: Small aquaculture technology supplier selling to farmers; limited marketing budget and weak F1 fit.

name: Engro Fertilizers
desc: Pakistan's leading urea fertiliser producer, selling Engro Zarkhez and other branded fertilisers to farmers through a dealer network.
markets: Sells fertiliser to farmers across Pakistan through dealers; subsidiary of Engro Corporation.
rationale: Strong Pakistani farm-input brand, but domestic customers and agricultural focus make an F1 partnership hard to justify.

name: DeHaat
desc: Agritech platform serving Indian farmers with seeds, fertilisers, advice, credit and market access through a network of village entrepreneurs.
markets: Operates across Indian states with farmers and village entrepreneurs; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic farmer platform with a rural audience; little F1 relevance beyond an India-awareness play.

name: Ecorobotix
desc: Makes AI-driven precision spraying robots, such as ARA, that spot-spray weeds and reduce herbicide use on farms.
markets: Sells to farmers in Europe and North America; venture-backed Swiss agtech.
rationale: Technology showcase possible for AI and robotics, but buyers are farmers and fit is modest.

name: Protix
desc: Rears black soldier fly larvae on food by-products and makes protein meal, fat and fertiliser for feed and pet food.
markets: Customers in animal feed, aquaculture and pet food in Europe and other regions; European production sites.
rationale: B2B sustainable-ingredient supplier; sustainability story suits F1 messaging, but customers are feed makers, so fit is limited.

name: Solinftec
desc: Develops the Solix agricultural robot and platform combining field sensors and weather data for sugarcane, soybean and corn farms.
markets: Customers are farms in Brazil, with operations also in the United States and other markets.
rationale: Ag-robotics technology brand with an international growth story; F1 technology showcase is plausible but customers are growers.

name: Green Plains
desc: Owns and runs US Midwest biorefineries producing ethanol, distillers grains, corn oil and renewable fuel ingredients.
markets: Plants in the US Midwest; sells ethanol and co-products to fuel blenders and feed buyers, with exports.
rationale: F1 is moving to sustainable fuels, giving a thematic link, but Green Plains is a commodity producer with little brand marketing.

name: Monarch Tractor
desc: Built the MK-V electric, driver-optional tractor for vineyards, orchards and small farms, sold with a software subscription.
markets: Sold to US specialty-crop growers; reports in 2025 pointed to severe financial difficulty and a wind-down.
rationale: Electric and autonomous technology fits F1 themes, but the company's financial position makes a partnership very unlikely.

name: Stacked Farm
desc: Australian farming company described as offering cost-effective nutritious food products; little else is confirmed.
markets: Based in Victoria, Australia; no confirmed customers, markets or expansion plans.
rationale: Apparently a small producer with no known marketing scale or international reach; weak F1 fit.

name: The Toro Company
desc: Makes turf maintenance, landscape, irrigation and snow equipment under brands including Toro, Exmark and Ditch Witch for professionals and homeowners.
markets: Sells through dealers and retailers in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Strong brand with global dealer network; F1 hospitality could reward dealers, though fit with motorsport is indirect.

name: Liberation Bioindustries
desc: Biotechnology company developing fermentation-based processes and bio-based chemicals; scale and products could not be confirmed.
markets: Based in New York; no confirmed customers, operations abroad or expansion plans.
rationale: Early-stage biotech with unconfirmed commercial scale and no known consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Locus Fermentation Solutions
desc: Makes sophorolipid biosurfactants and other fermentation-derived products for oil and gas, agriculture, cleaning and personal care customers.
markets: Sells biosurfactants to industrial customers in oil and gas, agriculture and consumer products; US base.
rationale: B2B specialty chemicals supplier, with an ESG positioning that could suit F1 sustainability messaging, but limited brand marketing.

name: Beewise
desc: Makes the BeeHome robotic, AI-driven beehive that monitors and treats colonies, rented to beekeepers and almond and fruit growers.
markets: Customers are beekeepers and growers, mainly in the United States, with deployments also in other countries including Israel.
rationale: AI and robotics showcase for farming; customers are growers, so F1 benefits are limited to technology credentials.

name: Carbon Robotics
desc: Makes the LaserWeeder, a tractor-pulled machine using computer vision and lasers to kill weeds without herbicides on farms.
markets: Sells to farms in the United States and other countries; venture-backed.
rationale: Computer-vision and AI technology story suits F1 tech showcase, but buyers are farmers, limiting commercial return.

name: ForFarmers
desc: Supplies compound animal feed and nutrition advice to livestock farmers in the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Belgium and Poland.
markets: Operations in the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Belgium and Poland; customers are livestock farmers.
rationale: B2B feed supplier selling to livestock farmers with no consumer brand; weak case for F1 sponsorship.

name: Oregon Tool
desc: Makes cutting tools for forestry, lawn and garden, including Oregon chainsaw chain and guide bars, sold to professionals and consumers.
markets: Sells through distributors and retailers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; manufacturing in several countries.
rationale: Tools brand with global dealer network; hospitality could support distributors, but motorsport link is indirect.

name: Cresud
desc: Owns and farms land in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay producing grains and livestock, and develops real estate.
markets: Farms in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay; listed in Buenos Aires and on Nasdaq.
rationale: Commodity farm operator with no consumer brand; F1 interest low, though Latin American growth gives minor appeal.

name: Baladna
desc: Qatari dairy and food company producing fresh milk, yogurt and juices, founded in 2017 for national milk self-sufficiency.
markets: Sells in Qatar and exports to other Gulf and nearby markets; Qatar Exchange-listed.
rationale: Consumer dairy brand in a region with F1 races; Qatar Grand Prix exposure could build brand awareness and export growth.

name: Itafos
desc: Produces phosphate fertiliser and specialty products from the Conda phosphate complex in Idaho and fertiliser assets in Brazil.
markets: Main operations in Idaho, USA; sells fertiliser mainly in North America, with an additional project in Brazil.
rationale: Commodity fertiliser maker selling B2B in North America; little case for F1 sponsorship.

name: Biotalys
desc: Develops protein-based biocontrol products for crop protection, led by Evoca for fruit and vegetables, sold to growers.
markets: Evoca approved in the US and sold to growers there; Europe registration pending; Euronext Brussels-listed.
rationale: Early-commercial agtech selling to growers; modest marketing budget, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Brazil Potash
desc: Developing the Autazes potash project in Amazonas, Brazil, intended as a domestic fertiliser source for Brazilian agriculture.
markets: Pre-revenue; planned supply is to Brazilian farmers, with no mine production yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue mining developer with a single project; no brand to market, weak F1 fit.

name: Coloured Ties Capital
desc: Calgary company tagged under agriculture and energy efficiency; no business description is available.
markets: Based in Alberta; no confirmed customers, operations abroad or expansion plans.
rationale: Little is known about the business; no evident brand or international reach for an F1 partnership.

name: Decibel Cannabis
desc: Calgary cannabis producer and brand house selling flower, vapes and edibles under consumer brands such as Qwest and Blendcraft.
markets: Sells licensed cannabis products in Canada; acquired by High Tide in 2024.
rationale: Cannabis marketing is restricted, and operations are Canadian only; F1 partnership is unrealistic.
changed: Acquired by High Tide in 2024

name: Nature's Miracle
desc: Designs and sells grow lights, hydroponic equipment and controlled-environment agriculture products to indoor growers.
markets: Sells to growers mainly in the United States; Nasdaq-listed small-cap.
rationale: Small equipment supplier with limited marketing resources and a narrow grower audience; weak F1 fit.

name: Galan Lithium
desc: Developing the Hombre Muerto West brine lithium project in Catamarca, Argentina, supplying lithium chemicals to battery makers.
markets: Operations in Argentina, with an Australian listing; offtake to battery supply chains.
rationale: Lithium supplier linked to EV theme, but a small developer selling B2B; F1 fit is weak.

name: Farmmi
desc: Produces and sells shiitake mushrooms and other edible fungi in dried, fresh and packaged forms, with exports.
markets: Sells in China and exports to Japan, South Korea, Europe and the US; Nasdaq-listed.
rationale: Small food exporter with modest marketing budget; F1 could lift brand awareness abroad, but fit is weak.

name: GreenFirst Forest Products
desc: Produces softwood lumber and other wood products at sawmills in Ontario and Quebec, sold to building-products customers.
markets: Mills in Ontario and Quebec; lumber sold to customers in Canada and the United States.
rationale: Commodity lumber producer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship has little commercial logic.

name: Sadot Group
desc: Trades agri-commodities such as soybeans, corn and wheat and operates restaurants, formerly known as Muscle Maker Grill.
markets: Physical commodity trading across several countries, plus US restaurant franchising; Nasdaq-listed small-cap.
rationale: Small commodity trader and restaurant franchisor with little brand scale; weak F1 fit for a sponsorship.
changed: Renamed from Muscle Maker Grill to Sadot Group in 2023

name: Rodnie Polya
desc: Russian company tagged under agriculture and fleet management; the Crunchbase description suggests trading and logistics of farm goods.
markets: Based in Rostov, Russia; no confirmed customers abroad or expansion plans.
rationale: Unconfirmed small Russian business; Russia-based companies are largely sanctioned from F1 sponsorship, so fit is very low.

name: Limagrain
desc: French farmer-owned cooperative group and one of the world's largest seed companies, with vegetable seeds, field seeds and bakery products.
markets: Seed businesses operate worldwide, including Vilmorin and Limagrain Europe, with bakery products under Jacquet Brossard.
rationale: Global farm brand with consumer bakery interests; F1 hospitality could help B2B relationships, though fit is limited.

name: Infarm
desc: Ran modular indoor farms in supermarkets and distribution centres growing herbs and leafy greens; it collapsed financially in 2023.
markets: Farms in Europe, North America and the Middle East were closed or sold after the 2023 insolvency.
rationale: Company collapsed after heavy losses and has shrunk to a minimal presence; no viable F1 case.
changed: Cut staff and closed most markets in 2023; insolvency of European units

name: Phibro Animal Health
desc: Makes medicated feed additives, vaccines, nutritional specialties and mineral products for livestock and poultry producers.
markets: Sells animal health and nutrition products in North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: B2B animal health supplier with global reach but no consumer brand; F1 is a weak fit.

name: Pivot Bio
desc: Sells microbial nitrogen products, such as ProveN and ProveN 40, that colonise corn roots and supply nitrogen to crops.
markets: Sells to US corn growers; no confirmed international operations.
rationale: Agtech sold to US farmers; sustainability story, but narrow audience and weak F1 fit.

name: Soli Organic
desc: Grows leafy greens and herbs in controlled-environment greenhouses and sells organic fresh produce to US retailers.
markets: Sells to US grocery retailers; no confirmed operations or expansion outside the US.
rationale: Small regional produce brand with a limited marketing budget and US-only presence; weak F1 fit.

name: Gotham Greens
desc: Grows lettuce, herbs and tomatoes in hydroponic rooftop and large greenhouses and sells packaged produce to US grocers.
markets: Greenhouses across US states supply grocery chains; no verified international operations.
rationale: Consumer-facing produce brand with a US-only retail footprint and moderate marketing; F1 fit is limited.

name: Little Leaf Farms
desc: Grows baby lettuce and leafy greens in large greenhouses using rainwater and sells them to US supermarkets.
markets: Greenhouses in the US Northeast and Pennsylvania supply supermarkets; no international activity.
rationale: US regional consumer produce brand with limited marketing scale; weak F1 fit.

name: eFishery
desc: Indonesian aquaculture technology company with smart feeders and a marketplace helping fish and shrimp farmers manage feeding and finance.
markets: Customers are fish and shrimp farmers in Indonesia, with some activity in nearby Asian markets.
rationale: A 2024 financial reporting scandal damaged the company, making a sponsorship unlikely.
changed: Financial reporting fraud revealed in December 2024, with leadership removed

name: Zhongxin Breeding
desc: Chinese pig breeding service provider supplying breeding pigs, semen and genetic improvement services to hog farms.
markets: Serves hog farms in China; no confirmed operations abroad or expansion plans.
rationale: B2B livestock genetics supplier selling to farms; F1 offers little commercial logic.

name: Atlas Agro
desc: Developing technology to make nitrate-based nitrogen fertiliser from air, water and renewable electricity, aimed at farmers.
markets: Pre-commercial; plans plants to supply farmers in several regions, with a Swiss base.
rationale: Pre-revenue clean-tech with sustainability credentials relevant to F1, but no consumer brand yet.

name: Finnforel
desc: Finnish fish farm that grows, processes and supplies rainbow trout to retailers and food service customers.
markets: Production in Finland supplying Finnish retail and food service; no confirmed exports.
rationale: Small domestic fish producer with a limited marketing budget and no known export brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Silo
desc: Provides software and financing for the produce supply chain, with inventory, order, logistics and payment tools for growers and buyers.
markets: Customers are US produce growers, distributors and retailers; no confirmed operations abroad.
rationale: B2B software for produce businesses; F1 hospitality could suit enterprise clients, but customer base is narrow.

name: First Water
desc: Farms Atlantic salmon in land-based tanks on geothermal land in Iceland for export to seafood markets.
markets: Single operating site in Iceland; salmon sold to export markets, with expansion within Iceland planned.
rationale: Premium fish farmer with minimal consumer branding and a single site; weak F1 fit.

name: Lygos
desc: Uses fermentation and synthetic biology to make bio-based specialty chemicals, such as malonic acid, as replacements for petrochemical products.
markets: Based in California; supplies chemical customers, with no confirmed operations abroad or expansion plans.
rationale: Venture-backed biochemical start-up selling B2B; sustainability angle fits F1 themes, but limited brand marketing.

name: Sonae Arauco
desc: Makes wood-based panels, including MDF, OSB, particleboard and laminate flooring, at plants in Portugal, Spain, Germany and other countries.
markets: Plants in Europe and Brazil serving furniture and construction customers; joint venture of Sonae and Arauco.
rationale: B2B panel maker with global manufacturing; F1 hospitality could suit customers, but there is little consumer branding.

name: Farmers Edge
desc: Provided farmers with satellite imagery, in-field weather stations and field-level analytics through a digital agriculture platform.
markets: Sold in Canada, the United States, Brazil, Europe and Australia; later ownership status could not be confirmed.
rationale: Digital farm software sold to growers; limited marketing budget and unclear current status.

name: Grow Up Farms
desc: Urban vertical farming company building farms in the UK to grow and sell fresh produce using clean energy.
markets: Farms in the UK; no confirmed operations abroad, and current trading status could not be verified.
rationale: Small UK produce farmer with limited brand reach and unverified current status; weak F1 fit.

name: Sound Agriculture
desc: Develops small-molecule crop products, such as SOURCE, that help plants take up nutrients, sold to growers.
markets: Sells to farmers mainly in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Agtech sold to growers; sustainability message but narrow B2B audience, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Agricola Cerro Prieto
desc: Peruvian agricultural company that produces and processes fruit; Crunchbase gives few details about its products or markets.
markets: Based in Peru; Peruvian growers typically export, but this company's markets are unconfirmed.
rationale: Likely a B2B fruit exporter with limited consumer branding; weak F1 fit.

name: InSoil
desc: Climate finance company that provides farmers with financing tied to climate-friendly farming practices.
markets: Based in Lithuania; target farmers are in Europe, but its exact markets are unconfirmed.
rationale: Small climate-finance start-up serving farmers; limited marketing budget, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Pairwise
desc: Uses CRISPR gene editing to improve food crops; its first consumer product was Conscious Greens, a less bitter mustard-greens mix.
markets: US-based; sells greens in US markets and licenses traits to food companies; no confirmed expansion abroad.
rationale: Biotech with a consumer product but small scale; F1 audience fit is weak.

name: L.B. Foster
desc: Supplies rail and infrastructure products including track components, friction-management systems and precast concrete products to railroads and transit operators.
markets: Customers are railroads and infrastructure owners, mainly in North America, with some presence in Europe.
rationale: B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit, other than rail-customer hospitality.

name: EagleNXT
desc: Makes eBee fixed-wing mapping drones and MicaSense multispectral sensors for agriculture, surveying and government customers; formerly AgEagle Aerial Systems.
markets: Sells drones and sensors in the United States, Europe and other markets; Nasdaq-listed small-cap.
rationale: Small drone maker with technology appeal, but limited budget and mostly B2B customers.
changed: Renamed from AgEagle Aerial Systems to EagleNXT in 2025

name: Red White & Bloom
desc: Cannabis multi-state operator formed by combining Tidal Royalty and Red White & Bloom, listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange.
markets: Operates licensed cannabis businesses in several US states; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Cannabis marketing is restricted and operations are US-only; F1 partnership is unrealistic.

name: Avanti Feeds
desc: Makes shrimp feed and processes and exports shrimp, serving aquaculture farmers in India and overseas buyers.
markets: Sells feed to Indian shrimp farmers and exports processed shrimp to the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B feed maker with some export branding and a limited marketing culture; weak F1 fit.

name: Davis Commodities
desc: Trades sugar, rice, edible oils and other staples to processors, wholesalers and traders in Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
markets: Customers in Asia, Africa and the Middle East; Nasdaq-listed small-cap based in Singapore.
rationale: B2B commodity trader without consumer brand; Singapore Grand Prix hospitality is the only angle.

name: Yimutian
desc: Operates an online agricultural trading platform and information service linking farmers with wholesale buyers through a mobile app.
markets: Platform serves farmers and wholesalers across China; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Domestic B2B farm platform with a narrow audience and limited marketing scale; weak F1 fit.

name: Twiga Foods
desc: Business-to-business supply platform buying fresh produce from farmers and delivering it to informal retailers and kiosks through a mobile app.
markets: Serves retailers and farmers in Kenya; earlier expansion to Uganda was later scaled back.
rationale: Local B2B supplier with limited marketing budget; Kenyan audience offers little F1 value.

name: Tongaat Hulett
desc: Produces sugar from cane in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Eswatini, plus starch and feed, and develops land in KwaZulu-Natal.
markets: Operations in southern Africa; sells sugar and starch locally and regionally; placed in business rescue in 2022.
rationale: Financially distressed commodity processor under restructuring with no consumer-brand budget; F1 sponsorship is unrealistic.
changed: Placed in business rescue in 2022

name: San Miguel
desc: Grows citrus, mainly lemons, and processes them into fresh fruit, juice, essential oils and pectin for export.
markets: Argentine citrus exported to Europe, the US and Asia; listed on Buenos Aires exchange.
rationale: B2B citrus processor with limited consumer branding and an Argentine base; F1 interest is weak.

name: Desert Control
desc: Sells Liquid Natural Clay, a clay-and-water spray that turns sandy soil into water-retaining soil for farms, golf courses and landscaping.
markets: Projects in Middle East, Africa, the US and Europe; Oslo-listed small company.
rationale: Small agtech company, but Middle East desert projects align with Gulf races; budget limits fit.

name: Pelican Aqua
desc: Cyprus-based company tagged under aquaculture and logistics; no further description is available.
markets: Based in Cyprus; markets, operations and any expansion plans are unconfirmed.
rationale: Almost nothing is known about the business; no evident basis for an F1 partnership.

name: Escorts Kubota
desc: Makes Farmtrac and Powertrac tractors, construction and material-handling equipment, and railway components; Kubota holds a major stake.
markets: Sells in India and exports tractors to many countries; Kubota partnership extends global reach.
rationale: Strong Indian machinery brand with growing exports; motorsport hospitality could support dealer networks, but F1 link is indirect.
changed: Renamed Escorts Kubota Limited in 2022

name: Neovia
desc: Produced animal nutrition premixes, feed ingredients and additives for livestock and pet food customers; now part of ADM.
markets: Served feed makers and farmers in many countries before integration into ADM Animal Nutrition.
rationale: Now merged into a larger group with sponsorship decisions elsewhere; little F1 logic as a standalone brand.
changed: Acquired by ADM in 2018 and merged into ADM Animal Nutrition

name: LIVEKINDLY
desc: Assembled plant-based meat and dairy alternative brands, including Oumph, Fry's Family Food, Like Meat and Wicked Kitchen.
markets: Brands sold in Europe, South Africa and North America; later restructuring and brand sales are not confirmed here.
rationale: Consumer food brands with a plant-based message; F1 sustainability themes fit, but the group has shrunk.

name: The Fynder Group
desc: Ferments a fungal microbe from Yellowstone into Fy protein, sold as meat and dairy alternatives under the Nature's Fynd brand.
markets: Sells products in US retail and food service; no verified international operations.
rationale: Consumer alternative-protein brand with sustainability story, but small scale and US focus limit F1 fit.

name: Resolute Forest Products
desc: Produces newsprint, market pulp, tissue, wood products and specialty papers for publishers and building products distributors.
markets: Mills in Canada and the US; customers in North America and exports to other regions.
rationale: Commodity paper maker now owned by Paper Excellence; no consumer brand and little F1 relevance.
changed: Acquired by Paper Excellence in 2023 and delisted

name: Pure Harvest Smart Farms
desc: Abu Dhabi agribusiness described as a tech-enabled farming company; little more is confirmed.
markets: Based in the UAE; markets and expansion plans are unconfirmed.
rationale: UAE location gives some access to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix hospitality, but the company's scale is unclear.

name: Anuvia Plant Nutrients
desc: Made enhanced-efficiency organic-based granular fertilisers from biosolids, including SC27, for farm and turf customers.
markets: Sold fertiliser to US growers and turf customers; current operating status could not be confirmed.
rationale: Small specialty fertiliser maker with a limited budget and unconfirmed operating status; weak F1 fit.

name: Tirlan
desc: Farmer-owned Irish dairy and agribusiness co-operative supplying farm inputs, operating dairy processing and marketing food ingredients.
markets: Irish milk and ingredients exported internationally; the society was formerly Glanbia Co-operative Society.
rationale: Farmer co-op with limited consumer branding; F1 hospitality is unlikely to suit members, so fit is weak.
changed: Renamed from Glanbia Co-operative Society to Tirlan in 2022

name: Molinos Agro
desc: Crushes soybeans and other oilseeds into meal and oil for export through Argentine port-linked plants.
markets: Exports soybean meal and oil from Argentina to global markets, mainly Asia and Europe.
rationale: Commodity oilseed processor selling B2B, with little brand marketing; F1 fit is weak.

name: GrowLife
desc: Sells hydroponic equipment, grow lights, nutrients and cultivation supplies to indoor growers through retail and online brands.
markets: US-focused company selling to indoor growers; current trading status and any foreign activity are unconfirmed.
rationale: Small cultivation-supplies seller with limited budget and unconfirmed trading status; F1 fit is weak.

name: Metsa Group
desc: Finnish forest industry group owned by Finnish forest owners through the Metsaliitto co-operative, making pulp, paperboard, tissue and wood products.
markets: Sells paperboard, pulp, tissue and wood products across Europe, Asia and North America.
rationale: Large Finnish industrial brand with global customers; sustainable-materials story suits F1, though sales are B2B.

name: Wilmar International
desc: Processes and trades palm oil, edible oils, sugar, rice, flour and oilseeds, with plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia.
markets: Operates in Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas, with consumer brands such as Fortune; Singapore-listed.
rationale: Large Asian agribusiness with consumer brands across Asia; F1 hospitality and Singapore Grand Prix give brand and B2B value.

name: Costa Group
desc: Grows and markets fresh produce, including berries, mushrooms, tomatoes, citrus and avocados, with farms in Australia, Morocco and China.
markets: Sells to supermarkets in Australia and exports; farms also in Morocco and China.
rationale: Produce supplier selling mostly to retailers; limited consumer branding, so F1 fit is weak.
changed: Taken private by Paine Schwartz Partners in 2024

name: FRD Japan
desc: Japanese company described as a technical environment firm in agriculture and food processing; no other detail is confirmed.
markets: Based in Saitama, Japan; customers, markets and expansion plans are unconfirmed.
